Conveniently import European Air Quality monitoring data into R

Source: R/import_eea_monitoring.R
import_eea_monitoring.Rd

This function is a convenient way to use EEA AQ monitoring data in an R session. It calls get_eea_parquet_files() or get_eea_parquet_urls(), reads each file using arrow::read_parquet(), removes unnecessary columns, and merges useful columns from import_eea_stations().

Usage

import_eea_monitoring(
  countries = "AD",
  cities = NULL,
  pollutants = NULL,
  datetime_start = as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")) - 1,
  datetime_end = as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")),
  dataset = 1L,
  aggregation_type = "hour",
  ...,
  .endpoint = c("files", "urls")
)

Arguments

countries

A vector of country codes from import_eea_countries(). Unlike the get_eea_parquet_*() family, at least one country must be provided.

cities

A vector of cities in the given countries from import_eea_cities(). If NULL, data from all cities in the given countries will be imported.

pollutants

A vector of pollutant notations or IDs from import_eea_pollutants(). If NULL, data for all pollutants will be imported.

datetime_start, datetime_end

Start and end date times, provided as POSIXct, Date or integer R objects.

  • A POSIXct represents an exact instant, and its timezone is respected.

  • A Date represents a whole day; datetime_end includes all of the given day, meaning providing the same Date to each will return a day of data.

  • An integer represents a whole year; datetime_end includes all of the given year, meaning providing the same integer to each will return a year of data.

Note that the EEA reports hourly data in UTC+01, so Date and integer inputs will define days and years in UTC+01 for hourly data, and in the local time of each station for daily data.

dataset

The dataset to use, as a single integer. One of:

  1. Unverified data transmitted continuously (Up-To-Date/UTD/E2a), covering the period not yet covered by verified data.

  2. Verified data (E1a) from 2013 onwards, reported by countries by 30 September each year for the previous year.

  3. Historical Airbase data delivered between 2002 and 2012, before Air Quality Directive 2008/50/EC entered into force. Note that Airbase uses different sampling point identifiers to datasets 1 and 2.

  4. CAMS forecasts, downscaled by the EEA to monitoring stations using a 1x1 km grid. Only available for PM10, PM2.5, O3 and NO2.

  5. Gap-filled E2a, using linear interpolation for smaller gaps, and a regressor based on similar stations for larger ones.

aggregation_type

represents whether the data collected is obtaining the values:

  1. Hourly data ("hour").

  2. Daily data ("day").

  3. Variable intervals (different than the previous observations such as weekly, monthly, etc.) ("var").

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

.endpoint

Which of get_eea_parquet_files() or get_eea_parquet_urls() to use. One of:

  • "files", which is subject to the EEA's 600MB download limit but only downloads data for the requested dates and aggregation_type.

  • "urls", which is not subject to the download limit, so can return much more data. However, it downloads the complete time series of each sampling point, which is then filtered to the requested dates and aggregation_type, so may be slower for short periods.

Value

a tibble. The date and date_end columns are POSIXct vectors which represent the correct instant in time. The EEA reports hourly and variable data in UTC+01 and daily data in the local time of each station; the timezone column records which of these applies to each row. If all rows share the same timezone, date and date_end will be displayed in it, otherwise they will be displayed in UTC.

Details

Note that the station metadata is obtained from a different source to the monitoring data, which may occasionally be unavailable. If so, a warning is given and the monitoring data is returned without site information (e.g., site, lat and lng), and daily data is assumed to be in UTC+01.
